headline: 3 PAVER
*MYTHS*
beats.vo: Three paver myths we hear all the time.
One: fabric stops joint weeds. Nope. Fabric keeps clay out of the base, but joint weeds grow from *seeds that blow in* on top.
Two: white haze means bad pavers. No. It's efflorescence. It's cosmetic and *it fades*.
Three: blast it with the pressure washer. Careful, that can *empty your joints*.
Topping up *polymeric sand*? It needs *dry pavers* and a *dry day*.
Which one did you believe? Comment below.

post.caption: 3 paver myths we hear around Metro Vancouver: fabric under the base doesn't stop joint weeds (the seeds blow in from above), white haze on new pavers is efflorescence and fades, and pressure washing can empty your joints. Topping up polymeric sand? Dry pavers and a dry day.
post.alt: Close-ups of tight paver joints on a pool deck, a paver walkway, a backyard patio and a soldier course beside river rock, with on-screen myth and fact text about joint weeds, white haze and pressure washing.
